citation: Drummond, K., Chinen, M., Duncan, T. G., Miller, H. R., Fryer, L., Zmach, C., & Culp, K. (2011). Impact of the Thinking Reader® software program on grade 6 reading vocabulary, comprehension, strategies, and motivation (NCEE 2010-4035). Washington, DC: National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education.
report_number: NCEE 2010-4035 (printed report number; later cataloged by IES as NCEE 2012-4036)
design: Multisite cluster RCT (Regional Educational Laboratory Northeast & Islands). Grade 6 reading/ELA teachers randomly assigned within school to intervention vs control (business as usual), after students were scheduled into intact classes. 32 high-poverty schools (>33% FRL) in 16 districts across CT, MA, RI; 92 teachers / 2,407 students at baseline; analytic sample 90 teachers and >=2,140 students. Intervention = Thinking Reader digital reading-comprehension software (3 digital novels) implemented after teacher professional development (two 6-hour group sessions + three individual coaching sessions, ~7.5-8.5 hrs) on the software and the three-phase instructional routine; used as a partial substitute for regular ELA instruction during the 2008-09 school year. Impacts estimated via 3-level HLM (students in teachers in schools), adjusted for student pretest, ELL & SpEd status, teacher education & experience, and school poverty & size. Subject = reading; grade 6 (registry grade band 3-6).
problems: Identification required tracing the abbreviated meta-analysis label 'Drummond et al. 2011' (registry 'Unpublished', goal 'TPD for digital tools', Teacher/Class RCT, grades 3-6, Res/Dev, Short, One arm) to this NCEE/REL report; web search confirmed Kathryn Drummond (AIR) as lead author. Note the registry codes the test as 'Res/Dev' (researcher/developer-made), but the achievement outcomes here are the Gates-MacGinitie Reading Tests (GMRT) vocabulary and comprehension subtests, which are a published standardized, independent instrument -> labeled standardized_independent (the registry 'Res/Dev' code may reflect that the digital intervention is researcher/developer-supplied, or a coding difference; flagging the discrepancy). Report number: the PDF/printed report and its own suggested citation say NCEE 2010-4035, while the IES pubsearch page catalogs it as NCEE 2012-4036 (April 2011); both refer to the same report. ICC: the only intraclass correlations stated (0.15 teacher-level, 0.15 school-level) are ASSUMED a priori power-analysis values (citing Schochet 2008), NOT empirically estimated design-effect ICCs from the study data, so icc is left null per spec (never guess/borrow an ICC); cluster_adjusted=true because impacts and SEs come from the 3-level HLM, so the design effect is already handled and no central ICC correction is needed. Two ancillary self-report outcomes (MARSI reading-strategy use ES=-0.00; MRQ reading motivation ES=-0.03) are metacognition/attitude self-reports, not academic achievement, so they were NOT extracted. Teacher-level / classroom-observation outcomes are not student achievement and were skipped. Single immediate post-intervention wave (spring 2009); no later wave.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Thinking Reader digital reading software (implemented after teacher PD/coaching) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Gates-MacGinitie Reading Tests (GMRT) Reading Vocabulary subtest, extended scale scores (45-item word-knowledge subtest)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's own Hedges' g: HG = beta01 / s_pooled, where beta01 = -1.24 is the 3-level HLM treatment coefficient (Table C3.1) and s_pooled = 34.86 is the unadjusted student-level posttest pooled SD (Table 4.1 footnote). d = -1.24/34.86 = -0.03557. df = n_t+n_c-2 = 2145, J = 1-3/(4*df-1) = 0.99965, so g = J*d = -0.0356 (report rounds to -0.04). Variance from the model-based (cluster-adjusted) SE: se_d = impact_se/s_pooled = 1.31/34.86 = 0.03758; g_se = J*se_d = 0.0376; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.001411. SE taken from the HLM, so it already accounts for clustering (students in teachers in schools).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.55 Table 4.1 (regression-adjusted means + ES); p.95 Table C3.1 (3-level HLM coefficient/SE); p.94 effect-size formula; Exec Summary p.5
effect_sizes.notes: Primary research question 1 (reading vocabulary). Estimated impact -1.24 (SE 1.31), p=.35, ns (Bonferroni-adjusted alpha=.025); 95% CI -4.17 to 1.69; report ES = -0.04. Regression-adjusted group means (extended scale scores): intervention 515.75, control 516.99. Analytic N for this subtest = 2,147 (intervention 1,156 / control 991), spanning 90 teachers in 32 schools. Negative sign = favors control (trivially). Sensitivity analyses (multiple imputation, fixed-effect treatment, two-level model, one classroom/teacher) did not change direction or magnitude.

effect_sizes.g_method: Report's own Hedges' g: HG = beta01 / s_pooled, where beta01 = 0.90 is the 3-level HLM treatment coefficient (Table C3.1) and s_pooled = 33.70 is the unadjusted student-level posttest pooled SD (Table 4.1 footnote). d = 0.90/33.70 = 0.02671. df = n_t+n_c-2 = 2138, J = 1-3/(4*df-1) = 0.99965, so g = J*d = 0.0267 (report rounds to 0.03). Variance from the model-based (cluster-adjusted) SE: se_d = impact_se/s_pooled = 1.72/33.70 = 0.05104; g_se = J*se_d = 0.0510; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.002603. SE taken from the HLM, so it already accounts for clustering.

effect_sizes.notes: Primary research question 2 (reading comprehension). Estimated impact 0.90 (SE 1.72), p=.61, ns (Bonferroni-adjusted alpha=.025); 95% CI -2.95 to 4.75; report ES = 0.03. Regression-adjusted group means (extended scale scores): intervention 507.42, control 506.52. Analytic N for this subtest = 2,140 (intervention 1,154 / control 986), spanning 90 teachers in 32 schools. One exploratory tertile interaction on comprehension was significant (5.77, p=.03) but treated as likely chance/post-hoc by the authors and is not the main impact contrast. Sensitivity analyses did not change direction or magnitude.
